A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Model Folding paper with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that substantive differences are confined to Table 3 and its caption.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression and model-merging experiments, LLM evaluations, ablations, and appendix measurements of accuracy, runtime, and memory.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for normalization-layer fine-tuning of folded LLaMA-7B.

M1.justification: Table 3 adds an optional post-folding procedure that fine-tunes LLaMA-7B normalization layers. The original untuned variant, clustering procedure, Fold-AR, and Fold-DIR remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses wikipedia_en as training data for normalization-layer fine-tuning of folded LLaMA-7B. This is a limited addition of training-data coverage; evaluation datasets, tasks, and appendix benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains magnitude pruning, LLM-Pruner, FLAP, Wanda_sp, SliceGPT, and ShortGPT as baselines. 'Magnitude Prune' becomes 'Magnitude Pruning' without changing the method. The new row is a variant of the proposed Model Folding method; other baseline comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a data-dependent normalization-layer post-tuning condition at 20% LLaMA-7B pruning, evaluated on the existing WikiText2 and four zero-shot tasks. Existing evaluation conditions and metrics are retained; the new tuning budget is unspecified.

E4.justification: The added Table 3 row supplies a limited comparison of folded LLaMA-7B with and without normalization-layer fine-tuning. Existing clustering, regularization, width, calibration-data sensitivity, and generated-text analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 adds no run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests. The new Table 3 row reports point estimates, and existing uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing results are unchanged. The new 20% pruning, normalization-tuned LLaMA-7B row reports WikiText2 perplexity 8.95, BoolQ 70.09, WinoGrande 63.14, ARC-e 59.85, ARC-c 28.24, and average 55.33. Untuned folding retains perplexity 13.33 and average 50.17; the added scores involve extra training, rather than a revised same-setting result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, clustering and variance derivations, assumptions, and appendix lemmas and proofs are unchanged. No theory accompanies the added fine-tuning experiment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-free, fine-tuning-free compression and its theoretical and empirical advantages. The optional Table 3 extension does not revise those main claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of variance preservation, calibration-data sensitivity, and limitations concerning redundancy and layerwise sparsity remain unchanged. The added caption reports improved performance after fine-tuning but supplies no new mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: The new experiment identifies the tuned components as layernorms and the training corpus as wikipedia_en. It provides no optimizer, learning rate, sample count, or training duration. Existing implementation, hardware, checkpoint, and code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Citations, references, related-work discussions, and positioning relative to prior compression and merging methods are unchanged, including Appendix M.

P1.justification: Edits comprise a short Table 3 caption extension, the 'Magnitude Pruning' label correction, and the arXiv version/date update. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains one row and a longer caption, shifting the following text downward on page 13. Its columns and other tables and figures, including those in the appendices, remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 comparison provides useful evidence about optional recovery through normalization-layer tuning when training data is available, while retaining the original untuned results. Its value is limited by missing tuning details and the retained 'without post-tuning' caption heading, which no longer describes every row. This is a modest empirical extension, not stronger evidence for the unchanged data-free procedure.
